title: Throttle Escort: failback gateway and statistical fairness playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During transient traffic spikes and partial limiter outages we produce two bad outcomes: (1) disproportionate shedding of lower-tier tenants due to coarse token windows, and (2) dangerous fail-open behaviour when central limiter leases expire without a safe fallback. This ticket proposes a lightweight fronting component ("Throttle Escort") and an operational playbook that: introduces a soft-escort queue that preserves tenant fairness using statistical quantiles, implements a deterministic failback path to regional rate authorities when global leases lapse, and coordinates circuit-breaker thresholds so downstream capacity is not overwhelmed. Goals: preserve SLOs for high-priority tenants, reduce 95th/99th tail latency regressions caused by heavy-handed shedding, and provide clear runbook actions for limiter outage recovery.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Throttle Escort can accept and classify incoming requests and route them to either immediate admission, soft-escort queue, or reject path under simulated overload. 2) Under replayed 10x burst tests, tenant fairness metrics (median/95th/99th of per-tenant admitted rate normalized by weight) improve by >=30% vs current baseline. 3) When global lease store becomes unavailable, requests seamlessly fall back to regional policy within 5s and no tiered tenant experiences >5% extra rejects beyond baseline. 4) Circuit-breaker engages and protects downstream model pools with no silent fail-open incidents during chaos tests. 5) New metrics and dashboards are available and validated in staging dashboards.
design_notes: - Concept: a thin, idempotent fronting gateway (Escort) runs colocated with edge proxies. It maintains soft state about short-term per-tenant arrival quantiles using streaming sketches (t-digest or KLL) and applies a probabilistic escort decision rather than hard token drops. - Escort queue: bounded priority queue ordered by tenant weight and recency; tokens can be admitted out-of-band by a background allocator that respects batchable model capacity. - Failback: region-local rate authority accepts temporary lease tokens when central lease manager is unreachable; leases are short (<=10s) and renewable. - Circuit breakers: multi-threshold design (warn/soft-stop/hard-stop) exposing exponential backoff headers for clients. - Fairness: use quantile-normalized admission probability: P(admit)=min(1, (weight * target_q / observed_q)). Track per-tenant q95 and q99. - Config: per-tenant weight, sticky routing to preferred region, emergency-only priority escalation for enterprise tenants. - Backwards compatibility: Escort proxies add headers but do not change existing auth flows. - Performance: Escort must add <0.8ms P50 CPU overhead at peak on a p4d edge node.
telemetry_changes: - New metrics: escort.incoming_rate, escort.escort_queue_length, escort.admit_rate_by_tenant, escort.q95_by_tenant, escort.q99_by_tenant, escort.failback_ratio, escort.circuit_breaker_state. - New SLO checks: dropped_by_weight_p95 and failback_latency_p95. - Alerts: failback_ratio > 0.05 for >2min, escort_queue_length > 90% capacity, circuit_breaker_hard_stop_count > 10/min. - Dashboards: per-region tenant fairness heatmap, long-tail admission latency, failback incidents timeline. - Links: Confluence design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Throttle+Escort+Design, dashboard draft https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/limiter/escort-staging
rollout_plan: 1) Canary: deploy Escort binary to 1 edge cluster, non-production traffic first. 2) Shadow mode: run Escort in decision-only mode for production traffic for 72h and collect metrics. 3) Soft enable: enable escort admission for 5% traffic with on-call kill switch. 4) Progressive ramp: 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% over multiple days while monitoring fairness metrics and SLO alerts. 5) Post-rollout: two-week observation window with daily review. 6) Runbook update: add step-by-step guide for emergency parameter changes.
rollback_plan: - Immediate: flip runtime flag to decision-only mode (Escort stops admitting into escort queue), which on its own reverts to current token-based limiter behavior. - If escort fronting causes unexpected downstream stress, circuit-breaker hard-stop escalation will proactively divert traffic; ops will then rollback service with the deployment pipeline (automated rollback tag). - Post-incident: hotfix to relax per-tenant admission probability, or reduce escort queue size. - All rollbacks must be communicated via #ops-incident and annotated in the incident ticket.
qa_plan: - Unit tests for admission math, quantile maintenance, and lease expiry. - Integration tests against local lease store and simulated region partition. - Load tests: 10k tenants with synthetic skew (Pareto alpha=1.2) and timed 10x bursts. Measure fairness improvement and tail latencies. - Chaos tests: kill central lease store mid-burst and assert failback within 5s. - Security: ensure header modifications do not leak secrets; run scanner.

open_questions: Which streaming sketch library should we standardize on across edge proxies? (KLL vs t-digest)
Exact emergency priority escalation rules for enterprise customers — per-customer opt-in or global flag?
Should failback leases be capped per-region to avoid global amplification of a regional outage?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Escort misclassification could increase tail latency. Mitigation: decision-only shadow mode and conservative initial admit probabilities.
Risk: Streaming quantile memory blowup for very high tenant cardinality. Mitigation: bounded sketches + tenant eviction LRU + sampling fallback for low-traffic tenants.
Risk: Complex rollout may introduce config drift. Mitigation: single runtime config with staged rollout and automated assertions in CI/CD.
